analysis:
Both units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1536-1982). The PR modifies only documentation: the patch replaces the v0.10.5 candidate header with a large new v0.10.6 section (head lines 11-808) covering two-Mac clusters, cluster_runtime registration facts, and pair-serving approvals. There is no executable code, configuration or schema change in the supplied evidence, so no concrete regression in code or controls can be shown from these units.

The BASE text I examined is historical changelog prose: SSD write endurance, cache reliability, App Attest, MDM freeze, erasure and similar topics. It is pre-existing and unchanged by the PR, so I do not restate it as new. It touches T-041 (the SSD prefix cache) and TB-011 (App Attest authorization), but the supplied hunk does not modify those descriptions.

Coverage limits and open integration questions: the head-side v0.10.6 text is truncated and unavailable here, and the patch excerpt is incomplete. The new cluster feature (RDMA over Thunderbolt between two Macs, cluster_runtime registration fields, pair-serving grants and approvals derived from releases) implies a new attack surface. That surface covers inter-Mac plaintext traffic carrying A-001 prompts, provider-reported cluster_runtime facts that are self-reported (relevant to T-034, T-054 and TB-011 trust in app-reported evidence), and a local API with a --local key. The canonical threat model has no TB or T entry for clusters. If the corresponding code changes appear in other batches, they need review against TB-002, TB-003 and TB-011, and the threat model may need a cluster boundary. Nothing in this changelog excerpt establishes a defect, so I am raising no finding, but deeper review of the code units is warranted.
